title: Rewrite `ELK` based on `GenericFileIOCalculator`
body:
This MR rewrites the `ELK` calculator based on `GenericFileIOCalculator`. This

- reduces the usage of `FileIOCalculator`
- simplifies the dependency of `ELK` (before both `FileIOCalculator` and `GetOutputsMixin`, now only `GenericIOCalculator` (as itself is a subclass of `GetOutputsMixin`))

According to the description in !2120, `ELK` probably does not have many users, and the core usage does not change (`test_elk.py` passes essentially as is).
I would therefore think it is OK to just replace the old `ELK` with the new one.

I guess `test_command.py` is not for `GenericFileIOCalculator` subclasses, so I removed the corresponding tests for `elk`.

The overhaul of `ELK` was also suggested in !2952. Since `git rebase` looked to me a bit complicated, I would just like to have a new clean one.

Closes !2952, #1030

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
Perhaps we should (although mostly for more commonly used calculators) provide a `command=None` parameter, and if it is not None, we show a warning/error with precise instructions?  We can also warn about ASE_ELK_COMMAND.  It probably doesn't matter much in this case though.

If we port calculators that are more widespread (e.g. Siesta) we should probably be more careful and provide them in a different module or with a different classname.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: I agree on both `command` and `ASE_ELK_COMMAND`, and in the revised commits, I followed how `Espresso` does.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @askhl for the review! For the suggestion, I followed accordingly.

Taking this chance, I also added a documentation and a small example for `ELK` (cf. #174, #1030).

During the survey I noticed a few related things:

- While the `species_dir` argument is used in `Elk`, internally Elk uses `sppath` for specifying the path to the species files.
It may therefore be natural to have it in `config.ini` with this name.

- At this moment we need to explicitly specify `tasks=0`, which indicates a single-point calculation. Probably we can set `tasks=0` for `write_elk_in` by default so that `Elk` works without any arguments by default. (Maybe soon in a separate MR.)
